# What Is a Modular Home? A Complete Guide for Today’s Homebuyers


Published On: September 28, 2026


•


11 min read


•


> **Quick answer:** A modular home is a house built in sections inside a climate-controlled factory, using the same materials, codes and standards as a site-built home, then transported and permanently installed on a foundation. It isn’t a mobile home or a kit — it’s a code-built house with a faster, more controlled construction process.


Did you know you can own a brand-new home, built to your style and taste and placed almost anywhere you want, for significantly less than a comparable site-built home? That price advantage is one reason more buyers are turning to modular construction.


At[Cavco](https://www.cavcohomes.com/) , our modular homes are built in modern, climate-controlled facilities using the same materials and standards as site-built homes, then finished on a permanent foundation. The result is a stylish, comfortable, long-lasting home delivered through a faster, more efficient — and more affordable — building process.


This guide covers what a modular home is, how it’s built, what it costs, and what to know before you buy. Along the way, we’ll share insight from our expert team.


Learn the differences between[modular homes, manufactured and mobile homes](https://blog.cavcohomes.com/what-is-mobile-manufactured-modular-homes/) .


## **What is a Modular Home?**


A modular home is a code-built home constructed in sections inside a climate-controlled facility, then finished on a permanent foundation. It’s built with the same materials, techniques and standards used in site-built construction — the difference is that the work happens indoors, in a controlled production environment, rather than outdoors on a job site.


At Cavco, our modular homes are built in our own facilities, where experienced teams follow consistent, assembly-line-style steps using modern tools and high-quality materials. This standardizes quality, improves efficiency, reduces waste and leads to steadier scheduling and predictable results — the same shift toward precision manufacturing that transformed other industries a century ago, now applied to homebuilding.


[Find Your Floor Plan](https://www.cavcohomes.com/find-a-floor-plan)


## **How Are Modular Homes Built?**


Modular homes are built in sections, called **modules** , inside our factories. Each module contains structural and mechanical systems – such as plumbing, electrical wiring, insulation, windows, interior finishes and cabinetry – installed and completed indoors. Once finished, modules are delivered to the home site and joined on a permanent foundation by professional builders who align, seal and finish the home.

Building indoors protects materials from weather and job site conditions, keeps lumber and fixtures secure, and helps avoid delays that often occur with outdoor construction. Because factory work happens at the same time the foundation is prepared, much of the process runs in parallel, shortening the full timeline so homeowners can move in sooner.


## **What Are the Benefits of Modular Homes?**


In short:


**quicker build times** ,


**high-quality construction** and a more


**affordable price** .


A modular home offers reliable construction, energy-efficient design and a smoother build experience. Cavco’s homes are framed, insulated and finished under one roof, which supports consistent craftsmanship from start to finish.


> “One of the biggest benefits is that they are built in a climate-controlled environment where materials and workers are not exposed to the elements,” says

## **How Long Does a Modular Home Take to Build?**


Depending on layout, size, design complexity and site prep, a modular home can be completed in as little as **10–12 weeks** , though **3–5 months** start to finish is more typical. That’s considerably faster than site-built construction, since our production facilities aren’t affected by weather or subcontractor delays.


Once the home is set on its permanent foundation, a local builder completes the final steps to make it move-in ready: roof sections are secured, exterior trim is finished, and modules are joined and sealed so the interior looks and feels like one unified home.


Licensed trades connect electrical, plumbing and HVAC systems to local utilities, and remaining interior work — flooring, cabinetry, paint and trim — is completed on-site. Exterior features like steps, porches or garages are added or finished to match the plan.


After final checks and inspections, the builder walks the home through with you, and it’s ready for move-in.


> **One thing to plan for:** your total timeline depends on more than the factory build — it also depends on how quickly your land and permits are ready. Buyers who already own land with utilities in place, or who choose a home already completed and available at a local retailer, often move in faster than those starting from raw land. Your[local Cavco retailer](https://www.cavcohomes.com/our-retailers/) can help you map out a realistic timeline for your specific site.


Depending on the layout, size, intricacies and design, and site prep, a modular home can be completed in as little as

**3 – 5 months** , start to finish. This is much quicker than site-built construction because our production facilities aren’t affected by weather or subcontractor delays.


Once the modular home is set on its permanent foundation, a local builder completes the final steps to make it move-in ready. Roof sections are secured, exterior trim is finished and modules are joined and sealed so the interior looks and feels like one unified home.


Licensed trades connect electrical, plumbing, and HVAC systems to local utilities, and any remaining interior work – such as flooring, cabinetry, paint and trim – is completed onsite. Exterior features like steps, porches or garages are added or finished to match the plan.


Afterward, the builder and inspectors complete final checks, a walkthrough is done with the homeowner and the home is ready for move-in.


### **Strength and High-Quality Construction**


The materials we use to build our modular homes — lumber, nails, flooring, fixtures — are high quality. Our crews use CAD (computer-aided design) to ensure accurate measurements and uniform assembly, and wall systems are secured with both nails and glue for added strength. Each home goes through a third-party inspection inside the factory and a local building inspection after installation — two layers of oversight many site-built homes don't get.


### **Energy Efficiency and Comfort**


Cavco homes use[energy-efficient](https://blog.cavcohomes.com/cavco-manufactured-homes-energy-efficient-and-affordable/) windows, insulation, ductwork and lighting, all installed in controlled conditions. Tight construction helps maintain indoor temperature and reduces overall energy use.


U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)


[research](https://www.huduser.gov/publications/pdf/factory.pdf) notes that controlled factory construction can improve air tightness and thermal performance, which can lead to lower energy use compared with site-built homes.


## **What Does a Modular Home Cost?**


Cavco does not publish fixed prices because of how many variables go into building a modular home that can affect price. These include size, layout, materials, location, land preparation and site work.


As a general starting point, a Cavco modular home typically runs about **15–20%** less than a comparable site-built home. According to


[industry data](https://www.angi.com/articles/modular-home-cost.htm) , all-in installed costs for an average modular home commonly range from roughly **$120,000** on the low end for a smaller, basic home up to **$300,000** or more for a larger home with premium finishes — with per-square-foot pricing varying widely by region and what's included.


That last point matters: **always confirm whether a quote covers just the factory-built home, or a full "turnkey" price** that includes delivery, foundation, utility hookups and site work. The two numbers can differ by tens of thousands of dollars, and comparing a bare home price to a turnkey site-built quote isn't an apples-to-apples comparison.


Economies of scale and our efficient build methods allow us to pass these savings along to our customers. If you’d like to get a personalized price quote,


[contact a Cavco retailer](https://www.cavcohomes.com/our-retailers/us) in your area.

## **How Do You Finance a Modular Home?**


Because modular homes follow local building codes and sit on permanent foundations, they qualify for the same financing as site-built homes, including conventional loans, U.S. Federal Housing Administration (FHA) loans, U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) loans, U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) loans and construction-to-permanent loans, including FHA One-Time Close.


[Local Cavco retailers](https://www.cavcohomes.com/our-retailers/us) help buyers understand their


[financing options](https://blog.cavcohomes.com/how-to-finance-a-manufactured-home/) and connect them with lenders familiar with factory-built housing.


> **Before you apply** , it helps to have three things in order: your credit profile, proof of income, and a clear picture of your land situation (owned outright, financed, or still to be purchased). If you don't already have land, many lenders can finance the land and home together in a single loan.


## **Where Can a Modular Home Be Placed?**


Modular homes follow the same local building codes as site-built homes, which gives them broad placement flexibility. They are installed on permanent foundations and inspected by local officials after the home is set. This aligns them with typical residential zoning requirements.


> “Typically, a modular home can be placed anywhere a site-built home can be built, since they are built to the same local and state building codes,” Terry says. “Of course, the site has to be able to accommodate the delivery and installation of the home.”


[Cavco retailers](https://www.cavcohomes.com/our-retailers/us) can assist buyers with site planning, permitting and any local guidelines that need to be considered, including grading, foundation type and utility access, which are worth budgeting for early rather than discovering mid-project..


## **How Do Modular Homes Perform Over Time?**


Daily living in a modular home feels the same as living in a site-built home because both follow the same codes, use the same materials and rely on the same systems. In fact, most people would never know the difference. That means long-term performance depends on routine maintenance and market trends, not the construction method – like any other home.


Across the broader market, modular homes built to local codes typically appreciate similarly to site-built homes in the same neighborhood.


## **Why Choose a Cavco Modular Home?**


A Cavco modular home offers a dependable build experience, flexible design choices and the comfort of a home built to the same standards as site-built construction – at a price that site-built homes simply can’t match.


> “What really sets Cavco modular homes apart from others is our unique designs and attention to detail,” Terry says. “In my opinion, it simply makes our homes look better and creates added value for the homeowner.”


Cavco’s factory-crafted process keeps materials protected, supports consistent workmanship and gives buyers confidence at every step. Our experienced home retailers can walk you through floor plans, site needs and financing options to help make your homebuying process easy to understand and enjoyable.

## **Modular Homes Frequently Asked Questions**


### **How is a modular home different from a manufactured home?**


Modular homes follow local building codes and are placed on permanent foundations. Manufactured homes follow the federal


[HUD Code](https://blog.cavcohomes.com/what-is-the-hud-code-for-manufactured-homes/) . ([Learn more](https://blog.cavcohomes.com/what-is-mobile-manufactured-modular-homes/) )


### **Can you customize a Cavco modular home?**


Yes. Floor plans, finishes, layouts and design features can be adjusted based on buyer preferences.


### **Are modular homes energy efficient?**


Yes. Cavco homes are built with insulation, windows and systems that support energy-efficient performance.


([Learn more](https://blog.cavcohomes.com/cavco-manufactured-homes-energy-efficient-and-affordable/) )


### **What financing options are available?**


Modular homes qualify for conventional, FHA, VA, USDA and construction-to-permanent loans.


([Learn more](https://blog.cavcohomes.com/how-to-finance-a-manufactured-home/) )


### **Do modular homes appreciate?**


Homes built to local codes typically appreciate according to general market conditions, similar to site-built homes.


([Learn more](https://blog.cavcohomes.com/do-manufactured-mobile-homes-appreciate-in-value/) )


### **Are modular homes inspected?**


Yes. Cavco homes undergo a third-party inspection in the factory and a local inspection after installation.
